Its not that there are no jobs, its that there are no "good" jobs that allow one to make a living sitting behind a desk, writing a few emails, making a couple of phone calls, and getting paid $90,000 a year. Most companies are looking to consolodate many of those types of jobs to fewer people who are provided with AI productivity tools. AI allows 3 people to do what used to take 10. However, just on the chance that there is a fundamental flaw in this strategy, companies are posting jobs. Sometime next year, as the AI question shakes out, the practice will cease, and we will either see a resumption of hiring, or a reduction in job postings.

I have opened several call centers in the Philippines. Customers in 2021 are still having a tough time adapting to bots because when they chat/speak with a bot, it can take 2 to 4 times longer to resolve an issue. Getting escalated to a human agent adds on more time which can be highly annoying. And what exactly do customers want first and foremost? They want a FAST resolution to any issues they have. Bots do help in some circumstances, but not all. The number of businesses that are outsourcing customer service and hiring human beings is still on the rise. Man, I hate this so much. KPI's have very little indication of how good you are at what you do, or how good you would be in a future role. Someone who is great at what they do will focus on what needs to be done for the group to be successful. Not what senior leaders, who haven't held a non-executive job this century, say your KPIs are. Poor KPIs can weed out bad individuals, but good KPIs will never highlight the individuals that shine.
